package_info.package_versions: unknown (multiple versions affected, as per public advisories)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised to include the Sunburst backdoor, which enabled attackers to gain unauthorized access to networks, exfiltrate data, and move laterally within affected organizations. The malicious code was inserted into legitimate software updates, making the entire package a vehicle for a sophisticated supply chain attack.

execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (maliciously modified DLL within the Orion platform)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code checks if it is safe to execute (anti-analysis), collects system and environment information, communicates with a command-and-control (C2) server, exfiltrates data, and executes commands received from the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs stealthy checks to avoid detection, establishes outbound network connections to attacker-controlled domains, exfiltrates sensitive information, and allows remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain code that communicates with external C2 servers, collects system information for exfiltration, or executes remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or update checks may contact vendor servers, but not in a stealthy, obfuscated, or command-execution manner.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the SolarWinds Orion DLL and distributed via software update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of backdoor code on customer systems

attack_chain.action: Backdoor code checks for safe execution environment and establishes contact with C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of system information and receipt of attacker commands

attack_chain.action: Backdoor exfiltrates data and executes attacker-supplied commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential lateral movement, data theft, or further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion processes
Orion DLLs making DNS queries to suspicious domains
Orion process executing commands or scripts not part of normal operation
Obfuscated or delayed execution logic within Orion DLLs
file_indicators: Presence of DLLs with known Sunburst IOCs
network_indicators: DNS queries to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion-related processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known Sunburst C2 domains. Check file hashes of Orion DLLs against known-good versions. Look for obfuscated or delayed execution logic in Orion DLLs. Use threat intelligence feeds to block or alert on known Sunburst IOCs at the network and file level.
